title: Natural Disasters

source.boundary: Actual Natural Disasters title lower right PDF7/printed25 through references upper left PDF12/printed30, before actual Bomb, Blast, and Crush Injuries title. Other chapters on these shared pages excluded.
source.verification: Selected vocabulary and chapter boundaries only; not clinical recommendations or current practice validation.

scope: Eighteen selected terms, not exhaustive chapter coverage. Offline candidate vocabulary, not medical anchors or image prompts. Newly recorded does not mean novel invention.

source_wording_notes.vectorborne disease: Source also uses vectorborne illnesses; disease occurs in Table6-2 and vectorborne infectious diseases in body on printed27.
source_wording_notes.amputation: Source has limb amputation on printed26.
source_wording_notes.crush injuries: Plural source wording; reuses singular Chapter5 crush injury cue.
source_wording_notes.blood banks: Plural source wording; reuses singular Chapter5 blood bank cue.

entries.cue: Mosquito riding a bold mathematical vector arrow.
entries.reason: A familiar biological carrier rides a mathematical vector. Mosquito is an exemplar, not the only vector or a disease-specific identifier.

entries.cue: Winged droplets travelling through the air between two mannequin faces.
entries.reason: Visual phrase assembly mirrors source wording. Not a modern aerosol/droplet classification, particle size, distance or isolation recommendation.

entries.cue: Recognizable cartoon microbes riding a tiny boat on water.
entries.reason: Boat and water make borne/carried memorable. Not a pathogen, route-specific diagnosis or claim that any water is infectious.

entries.cue: Gaunt study mannequin reaching into an empty lunchbox.
entries.reason: Familiar deprivation cue, not diagnostic appearance, a comprehensive definition or a statement that all malnutrition causes thinness.

entries.cue: Empty medicine bottle visibly being refilled.
entries.reason: Simple action is more useful than a forced pun. Does not encode the medicine, quantity, substitution or prescribing decision.

entries.cue: Taut vessel model under a pressure gauge whose needle points high.
entries.reason: High pressure and tension provide a learned cue. Not a diagnostic measurement, pressure threshold or literal complete mechanism.

entries.cue: Outside scaffold visibly connected to and bracing a broken-bone model across its gap.
entries.reason: External support relation is recognizable without a strained phonetic construction. Not device anatomy, placement or treatment selection.

entries.cue: Small tsunami wave entering a lung silhouette.
entries.reason: Compact source-phrase association, not a diagnostic image, complete pathophysiology or equivalence to every drowning-related lung injury.

entries.cue: Portable generator with exhaust trapped inside an enclosed miniature room.
entries.reason: Generator is explicitly discussed in this source. Contextual learned cue, not unique gas identification or a diagnosis. Draw exhaust context without depicting carbon monoxide itself as visible colored gas.

entries.cue: Two separated bone-end characters with wedding rings turn away from each other, arms folded, with a clear gap between them.
entries.reason: Marriage union gives a double meaning; visibly turned-away postures express refusal rather than relying on narration. Not a healing timeline, imaging criterion or proof that any separated fracture is nonunion.

entries.cue: Detachable study-mannequin limb removed and set apart from its body.
entries.reason: Familiar visual category avoids forcing an amp sound fragment. Not a procedure, indication or claim that removal is always traumatic.

entries.cue: Submerged mannequin reaching toward the water surface.
entries.reason: Useful learned situational cue, not a diagnosis or assertion that drowning always looks like visible struggling.

entries.cue: Soot-darkened damaged airway model with airflow visibly directed inward.
entries.reason: Inward airflow and damage carry the association. Smoke is one exemplar, not all inhalational injuries, and visible soot is not a required diagnostic sign.

entries.cue: Kidney-shaped factory with conspicuously broken gears.
entries.reason: Reuse established candidate rather than remap kidney failure. Not mechanism or diagnostic criteria.

entries.cue: Limb mannequin compressed in a large vise.
entries.reason: Reuse Chapter5 compression cue; no duration, syndrome definition or treatment.

entries.cue: Additional open care spaces facing a wave of arrivals.
entries.reason: Capacity remains visible, not merely a crowd. Reuse rather than new discovery.

entries.cue: Bank vault holding recognizable blood bags.
entries.reason: Established vault cue, not storage, supply or transfusion instructions.
No economical bridge proposed; sofa/onion fragments would require too much sound repair. Hold is not proof that a useful bridge cannot exist.
